data.narrative:
Critical Energy, founded by Spencer Jackson, is a Seed-stage climate and energy company that has raised $22M to date. The target operates within a sector comprising one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private peers, including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen.

Valuation triangulation relies on a single applicable method given data constraints. Stage-progression analysis applies a 2.5x multiplier to the $22M total raised, reflecting typical step-up dynamics from Seed to subsequent funding rounds, yielding an implied valuation of $55M. A peer-median approach was not applicable; while nine same-sector comparables exist in Climate & Energy, insufficient narrow-stage and similar-tier peers met the minimum threshold of three datapoints required for meaningful median derivation, making sector-wide aggregation unreliable for this stage-specific analysis.

The triangulated valuation range is $47M (low) to $63M (high), with a median of $55M. This analysis rests heavily on stage-progression methodology, introducing material dependency on the assumed multiplier. Key uncertainties include the absence of direct peer-stage transaction data, which would improve specificity, and the limited public comparables in the energy technology sector. Further validation through operational metrics (burn rate, runway, customer concentration) or additional financing signals would strengthen confidence in this range.
